source_refs.note: Topic 8.9, printed pages 176-179; Sample Problems 8.3 and 8.4 and Quick Check 8.5 as the self-check.

blocks.text: Four kinds of quantity can be used to write the equilibrium constant of a reversible reaction aA + bB giving cC + dD: concentrations in mol dm-3 give Kc = [C]^c [D]^d / [A]^a [B]^b; partial pressures of gases give Kp = pC^c pD^d / pA^a pB^b; numbers of moles give Kn = nC^c nD^d / nA^a nB^b; and mole fractions give Kx = xC^c xD^d / xA^a xB^b. The constants are related by Kp = Kc (RT)^delta n, Kp = Kx (P)^delta n and Kp = Kn (P/N)^delta n, where R is the gas constant, T the absolute temperature, P the pressure of the system, N the total number of moles of reactants and products, and delta n the difference between the moles of products and of reactants in the balanced equation. Which constant is bigger depends on delta n; if the mole numbers of reactants and products are equal, delta n = 0 and Kp = Kc = Kx = Kn, so whichever units are used the constants are the same.
Sample Problem 8.3: Kc to Kp for ammonia

At 500 degrees C the Kc of N2(g) + 3H2(g) giving 2NH3(g) is 6.0 x 10^-2. T = 500 + 273 = 773 K, R = 0.0821 dm3 atm K-1 mol-1, and delta n = 2 - 4 = -2. Kp = Kc (RT)^delta n = 6.0 x 10^-2 x (0.0821 x 773)^-2 = 6.0 x 10^-2 x (63.5)^-2 = 0.06 / 4032.25 = 1.4 x 10^-5; Kp is less than Kc.
Sample Problem 8.4: Kp from partial pressures

For 2SO2(g) + O2(g) giving 2SO3(g) the equilibrium partial pressures are SO2 1.0 x 10^6 Pa, O2 7.0 x 10^6 Pa and SO3 8.0 x 10^6 Pa. Kp = pSO3^2 / (pSO2^2 x pO2) = (8.0 x 10^6)^2 / ((1.0 x 10^6)^2 x 7.0 x 10^6) = 9.1 x 10^-6 Pa-1.
